name: Northern Beardless-Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Southeastern arizona to southern texas, western mexico, and northern costa rica; cozumel
description: Tiny flycatcher found in Mexico and Central America. In the U.S.

name: Diademed Tanager
rangeDescription: Paraguay to southeastern brazil, uruguay, and northeastern argentina
description: Large blue tanager with a short strong bill. Unmistakable; mostly blue with a black mask, a red crest, and a white crown.

name: Cuban Blackbird
rangeDescription: Cuba including isla de la juventud (isle of pines; south of western cuba)
description: A vocal, gregarious inhabitant of many habitats, although avoids dense woods; often found near human habitation. Note the glossy purple-black plumage, medium-length squared tail, and somewhat thick bill.

name: Kea
rangeDescription: Mountains of south island (new zealand)
description: The world's only true alpine parrot, found only on the South Island of New Zealand. Large, with olive-green plumage.

name: Indigo Bunting
rangeDescription: Canada and usa; winters to greater antilles, colombia, and venezuela
description: Breeding males are entirely blue with a slightly darker head. Females are plain brown with a whitish throat, bluish tail, and faint streaks on the underparts.

name: Buru Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Mountains of buru (southern moluccas)
description: A medium-sized, largely olive-brown songbird with a striking yellow base to the downcurved bill, a thin yellow line from bill to eye, and dull bare skin behind the eye. Found in foothills and mountains, within forest, forest edge, and scrub as singles and pairs, and also joins mixed-species flocks.

name: Puerto Rican Tanager
rangeDescription: Highlands of puerto rico
description: A noisy, gregarious species of middle to high elevation forests where it often forms mixed-species flocks. Typically roosts communally in palm or bamboo thickets.

name: Ibadan Malimbe
rangeDescription: Savanna of southwestern nigeria
description: A striking black-and-red forest malimbe. Male has a black face and a red crown, nape, neck, and breast; female similar, with a narrower breast band.

name: Elegant Imperial-Pigeon
rangeDescription: Small islands off moluccas to eastern lesser sundas
description: A large pigeon of small islands. Shows a conspicuous pale yellow eye, a pale gray head and underparts, a chestnut vent, and a green back, wings, and uppertail.

name: Red-and-white Spinetail
rangeDescription: Far southeastern colombia to eastern peru and amazonian brazil
description: Strikingly bicolored spinetail, bright rusty above and white below. Note the dusky lores.

name: Creamy-bellied Thrush
rangeDescription: Eastern peru to central argentina, paraguay, uruguay, and brazil
description: Brownish thrush found commonly in a variety of habitats including forest edges, woodlands, savannas, plantations, urban parks, and gardens. Generally, quite arboreal but can be seen on the ground.
imageCreditName: João Vitor Andriola | Brazil Birding Experts

name: Red-naped Fruit-Dove
rangeDescription: Forest of sumba (western lesser sundas)
description: A large, striking fruit-dove with a dark lower body, a cream-colored head, and a diagnostic conspicuous red patch on the nape. Juveniles show yellow fringes to upperparts feathers and greenish feathers on head and breast.

name: Samoan Island-Thrush
rangeDescription: Samoa (savai'i and upolu)
description: Dark thrush with orange bill, eyering, legs, and feet. Endemic to Samoa, where found only at the highest elevations and generally not often encountered.

name: Orange-bellied Antwren
rangeDescription: Eastern brazil (eastern alagoas and eastern pernambuco)
description: Small canopy antwren, unmistakable in its tiny range. Males have a gray back, gray head, black-and-white streaked flanks, and white underparts.

name: Chestnut-shouldered Antwren
rangeDescription: Eastern ecuador to northwestern bolivia and southwestern amazonian brazil
description: Small canopy antwren. Gray head, with yellowish underparts, and wingbars; males have a fine black eyeline and cap.

name: Lesser Whistling-Duck
rangeDescription: Indian subcontinent to southeastern asia and greater sundas
description: A small, well-proportioned, tree-nesting duck. Pale brown overall with a darker brown crown and nape, warmer chestnut underparts, and chestnut-fringed feathers on the back.

name: Citron-headed Yellow-Finch
rangeDescription: Highlands of western bolivia and northwestern argentina (jujuy)
description: Striking and beautiful terrestrial finch-like tanager of the high Andes of central and southern Bolivian and extreme NW Argentina. Yellow head and mid chest and belly, contrasting sharply with mostly gray plumage, is distinctive.

name: Palawan Tit
rangeDescription: Southwestern philippines (balabac, calauit, and palawan)
description: A small bird of wooded areas on Palawan and neighboring islands, with a full black hood, yellow underparts, a black wing with two white wing-bars and edges, and a black tail with a white tip and outer tail feathers. Back is bright yellow in males and olive in females.

name: Black-capped Piprites
rangeDescription: Locally from southeastern brazil (rio de janeiro) to northeastern argentina
description: Small and chunky manakin-like flycatcher with a short bill and big eyes. Mostly rusty with a black crown, a yellow bill, and yellow-edged flight feathers.

name: Flat-billed Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Western samoa (apolima, upolu, and savai'i)
description: A compact kingfisher with a comparatively short, shallow, wide bill. Has deep blue wings, a greenish-blue back, and a blue cap with buffy white in front of the eye that narrows above it to form an eyebrow.
